items.title: Mississauga singing sisters win top prize at Canadian National Exhibition competition
items.summary: Mississauga sisters took a top prize at the Canadian National Exhibition’s Rising Star Talent Competition. Teenage vocalist siblings Catherine and Chloe Tiongson competed against 84 contestants in their age group and won the Youth Grand Champions title during the final weekend of Canada’s largest fair, the CNE said. While the pair have entered the competition before, this was the first time Chloe, 16, and Catherine, 13, have combined their talents in a duet. The pair chose the song And I Am Telling You by Henry Krieger and Tom Even, made famous by Jennifer Hudson in the film Dream Girls and Amber Riley in the first episode of the TV show Glee. The song is strong and powerful, said Catherine. Normally a solo song, they chose to sing it together, and the blending and chemistry on stage came naturally, said Chloe. “I think our voices complement each other,” said Catherine. items.title: Voters urged to cast their ballots early in Mississauga: city
items.summary: Mississauga residents planning to vote in the upcoming municipal election are being urged to cast their ballots early. The City of Mississauga says people don’t have to wait until election day, Oct. 26, to choose their preferred candidates in the races for mayor, 11 city council seats and trustee positions at both school boards. Eligible voters in Mississauga can make their selections in advance at any number of locations across the city between Oct. 6 and Oct. 11. They can do so at Mississauga City Hall on Oct. 6-7 and at various other spots from Oct. 8-11. “Advance voting gives voters more days and more locations to cast their ballot before election day,” the city said, adding it’s the same voting process, just offered earlier to allow voters to choose a time that works best for them. “Advance voting helps make voting easier, reduces lineups and gives voters more flexibility. If you have work, school, caregiving responsibilities, travel plans or other commitments on Oct. ” For those who wait until election day to cast their ballots, they must do so at a voting location in the Mississauga ward in which they live or own property. Those voting in the upcoming election must bring along their voter notification card, if they’ve received one, and one piece of acceptable identification, city officials said.

items.title: House of the week: Family home with classic features in Mississauga
items.summary: This place: A family home with classic features in Mississauga. Features: This timeless family residence is nestled in the heart of Central Erin Mills. A grand foyer makes a memorable first impression with checkerboard ceramic tile floors. Hardwood flooring and crown moulding extend through the formal living and dining rooms. The kitchen boasts stainless steel appliances, quartz countertops, cabinetry and checkerboard ceramic tile flooring. The bright breakfast area has a walkout to the backyard patio. Overlooking the kitchen, the family room features a gas fireplace, chair rail detailing, pot lights and large windows framing views of the front yard. Completing the main level is a versatile room suited as a home office, library or playroom. Upstairs, the skylight lit staircase leads to the primary bedroom with a walk-in closet and a five-piece ensuite bathroom featuring double sinks, a Jacuzzi tub and a walk-in shower. Three additional bedrooms each offer closet space and one has a four-piece ensuite bathroom, while the remaining two share a five-piece bathroom. The finished basement features a recreation room, a fifth bedroom and a four-piece bathroom.

items.summary: Join us on October 1 for Homegrown Mississauga: Apples, Art & Seed Saving, a free community event that celebrates local food, gardening and public art. Growing food, whether in a backyard, on a balcony, or in a community garden, brings people together and helps make our city greener and more resilient to the impacts of climate change. items.title: VIA Rail's plan to cut Guildwood, Malton service and reduce eastern Ontario trains sparks outcry
items.summary: The Crown corporation says the changes will roll out Oct. 25 and affect routes along the Ottawa-Toronto corridor. VIA Rail will be rolling out its new schedule on Oct. 25. Via Rail says it will no longer serve Toronto-area stations Guildwood and Malton later this fall as it rolls out multiple adjustments and reduced train service along select routes. The upcoming changes, announced Wednesday and set to begin Oct. 25, will also affect service along the Ottawa-Toronto corridor, including stops in Kingston and Cobourg, sparking sharp criticism from municipal leaders. m. train from the nation’s capital to Toronto. “The revised schedule will better align service with passenger demand, strengthen network resilience and support more reliable and predictable service,” Via Rail wrote in a news release. Via Rail said the removal of stops at Guildwood in Scarborough and the Malton in Mississauga will “improve overall travel times,” citing the stations’ proximity to Union Station in downtown Toronto and the availability of GO Transit and other services. Scarborough councillor and Toronto deputy Mayor Paul Ainslie slammed VIA’s decision, calling on the transit agency to reverse it.

items.title: ‘Residents heard loud & clear’: Mississauga council unanimously approves one-year moratorium on AI data centres
items.summary: Forty-nine days after first moving to freeze new approvals, Mississauga has officially hit pause on large-scale data centre development for one year, to study the environmental and social impacts of one of the fastest-growing pieces of the voracious digital economy. That is what Ward 9 Councillor Martin Reid told residents gathered at Mississauga City Hall Wednesday morning, moments before council voted 10-1 to make the decision without hearing from members of the public who had hoped to address the future of data centres in the city. Ward 7 Councillor and mayoral candidate Dipika Damerla was the only member who voted against the motion brought forward by Mayor Carolyn Parrish to move directly to a vote on the interim control bylaw (ICBL) — bypassing the 21 delegates who had come to City Hall to speak on the issue. Though Damerla and residents supported the central issue that was approved moments later, they disagreed with the decision to cut out the public from further debate before the eventual decision was made. “I dislike the idea that people were denied the ability to speak their voice,” resident George Tavares, who registered to delegate and is also running for Ward 7 in the upcoming elections, told The Pointer. ” Tavares fears residents who registered to delegate on the ICBL but did not get the opportunity to speak because council moved directly to a vote could potentially be subject to Council Procedure By-law 0044- 2022's 12-month restriction on speaking on the same subject again. The City confirmed that the bylaw provision won’t apply to the residents since “they did not speak” at the council meeting. “They can speak on this topic in the future,” a spokesperson clarified.
